headline: Maryland Awards $43M in Solar Grants to Help 4,800 Low-Income Families
meta_description: Maryland announces 69 community solar grants worth $43 million, cutting electricity bills by at least 25% for over 4,800 low-income households.
summary_short: Maryland is distributing $43 million in community solar grants to slash electricity costs for thousands of families struggling with energy bills.
body:
Maryland has announced 69 community solar grants worth $43 million, a move designed to cut electricity bills by at least 25% for more than 4,800 low-income households across the state.

The initiative goes further still: another 1,000 households will receive energy assistance as part of the program. Community solar allows families to benefit from shared solar installations without needing rooftop systems of their own—a critical advantage for renters and those in multifamily housing who cannot install traditional solar panels.

The grants represent a direct response to the energy cost burden borne by low-income families, many of whom spend an outsized portion of their income on utilities. By bringing solar economics to scale across 69 separate projects, Maryland is making clean energy accessible to households that have historically been left out of the solar revolution.
quick_facts: 69 community solar grants distributed across Maryland
$43 million total investment in the program
At least 25% electricity bill reduction for participants
